tests.title: Q2991 repeatedly destroys real Vue 2 instances and subscriptions without retaining connected Realms

issues.conditions: Vue 2.7.16 real component mounts/clicks/disposes four times; destroyed hook count, event subscription release, iframe disconnection and DOM cleanup checked each cycle. Vue destroyed hook sends an acknowledged service call; async unmount awaits it before MessagePort teardown. This avoids treating queued fire-and-forget teardown events as synchronous evidence.
issues.limitations: Does not prove garbage collection, bounded heap growth, original 32-bit Windows Chrome memory behavior or absence of retained detached objects; explicit saved iframe references in probe intentionally prevent heap reclamation measurement.

tests.title: W1057 configured load timeout removes a delayed entry Realm and permits recovery at the same URL
W1057 HTML script timeout cancels transport and recovers at the same URL
W1057 HTML stylesheet timeout-only releases Runtime resources with native transport remaining pending

issues.conditions: Module timeout probe plus real HTML external classic script and CSS served by node:http. Runtime load timeout rejects and removes Realm/surface. Classic script branch asserts physical transport close and same-URL recovery with clicks/CSS color. Stylesheet branch asserts only timeout/DOM cleanup and records transport limitation; it makes no CSS recovery assertion.
issues.limitations: Native control 9 cases (3 engines × remove link / clear href / remove ShadowRoot host) observed no stylesheet transport cancellation within 5000ms. CSS waiting/DOM cleanup and recovery are tested; physical CSS transport cancellation is not claimed. See native-network.json/log and archived native-network.spec.ts.txt. Real Safari not executed. Chromium/Firefox reuse a still-pending identical CSS URL, so same-resource recovery timed out (runtime-network-final.json). Verified recovery uses the same HTML entry with an explicitly new CSS revision query; the old response remains open until fixture teardown and is never claimed cancelled. Versioned-CSS recovery attempt also times out in Firefox (runtime-network-verified.json); Chromium/WebKit pass that narrower recovery. No physical CSS cancellation or all-engine CSS recovery claim is justified.
issues.executionNote: Final timeout-only test source and renamed titles not rerun by subagent; root must bind new titles only after actual final verification. Existing failed reports retained; this is an evidence-backed test contract correction, no product fix.
issues.archiveNote: Versioned recovery source copied verbatim before final contraction. Original same-CSS recovery source reconstructed by reverting only the versioned CSS URL / new request-evidence additions; historical actual execution remains runtime-network-final.json/log (exit 1). Native source copied before removal.
